facts.claim: "Red Wine Supernova" was written by Chappell Roan, Lisa Hickox, Amy Kuney, Dan Nigro and Annie Schindel, and produced by Dan Nigro.
WhoSampled credits Noah Conrad and Lixa as producers alongside Dan Nigro.
It was released as a single on 19 May 2023, ahead of the album The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess.

Roan told Zane Lowe she needed a campy gay girl song that captured the magic of having feelings for another girl. She said she packed it with fun raunchy lyrics that feel like a night out flirting with the girl across the bar.
The song took about three years to finish. It began in 2019 as a melancholic ballad, and Dan Nigro helped turn it into a silly, celebratory anthem.
Roan shared the original demo on TikTok and said it came from her "straight" era. The original cut was a ballad with no explicit references to girls.
Roan described the song as the gay girl version of Oasis's "Champagne Supernova".
Nigro and Roan added the bridge and expanded the instrumentals. Roan has said the song was written with live performance in mind, especially the audience-interaction bridge.
Chappell Roan was born Kayleigh Rose Amstutz in Willard, Missouri. She began writing songs at 12, signed with Atlantic Records at 17, and released her debut EP School Nights in 2017.
The album was released on September 22, 2023 by Amusement Records in partnership with Island Records. It was developed mainly with producer Dan Nigro.

research.lineage: A campy, queer, synth-driven dance-pop anthem that reframes Oasis's Britpop-era "Champagne Supernova" through a sapphic lens.

draft:
Halfway through its come-on, **Red Wine Supernova** stops to correct itself. The narrator brags about a California king at home, then backs down: "Okay, maybe it's a twin bed." There are roommates too. The lie lasts about one breath before honesty wins, and that small climbdown is the song's whole personality. This is flirting as a performance that keeps cracking, and the cracks are where the feeling gets in.

Chappell Roan told Zane Lowe she wanted a campy gay girl song about the magic of having feelings for another girl, packed with raunchy lines that play like a night out flirting with someone across the bar. She has called it the gay girl version of Oasis's "Champagne Supernova." The swap of champagne for red wine says a lot. The cosmic Britpop title comes down to bar-stool scale, and the borrowed grandeur turns into a wink.

The song wasn't always a wink. It started in 2019 as a melancholic ballad from what Roan called her "straight" era, with no explicit mention of girls. It took about three years and producer Dan Nigro's help to become a celebration. You can still hear the ballad in the chorus's lead-in: "Fell in love with the thought of you / Now I'm choked up, face down, burnt out." That's a heartbreak line, and it sits right before the narrator asks the girl to come over. Longing and nerve share the same breath, and the song never decides which one is winning. The bravado (the go-go boots, the Bardot fantasy, the shrug at her being a stoner) reads as a way to survive wanting someone this much.

The arrangement gives that nerve a floor to stand on. A four-on-the-floor kick and a backbeat clap keep things steady and mid-tempo. A bright synth pad holds the chords while a clean electric guitar picks out arpeggios, and the bass stays simple. Roan's voice is clear and a little breathy, held long on the sustained notes, with stacked harmonies swelling around it. The hi-hats get busier as the song builds, and the whole thing is polished and bright, more dance floor than dive bar.

Roan has said the song was written with live performance in mind, especially the bridge, the twin-bed confession and the bawdy magic-trick joke that Nigro helped add. It is built for a crowd to shout back. That turns a private crush into a room full of people saying the embarrassing part out loud together.

The song lets you be brave and mortified at once, and it makes the mortified part the most fun to sing.

factCheck.claim: Halfway through its come-on, the song stops to correct itself (the California king / twin bed turn).
factCheck.note: 'Halfway' is a claim about where the moment falls in the song, and the lyrics' structure puts it late, after the second chorus. Reworded to 'Mid-pitch', which makes no positional claim.

factCheck.claim: "Okay, maybe it's a twin bed." The narrator first brags about a California king, and there are roommates too.
factCheck.note: Quote matches the lyrics exactly. The California king and roommates are in the lyrics.

factCheck.claim: Roan told Zane Lowe she wanted a campy gay girl song about the magic of having feelings for another girl, packed with raunchy lines that play like a night out flirting across the bar.
